theory.intro: Real shapes like tents, sails and bridge trusses are rarely one labelled right-angled triangle. Find the right-angled triangles inside the shape. If one has enough information, solve it and carry that result into the next; otherwise, form and solve an equation involving both triangles.
facts: An identified right-angled triangle has enough information for a numerical trigonometric calculation when a side and an acute angle, or two sides, are known. If neither triangle has enough information, use their shared lengths and the given total or gap to form and solve an equation involving both triangles.
A total length, such as a perimeter, a span or a gap, is the **sum or difference** of lengths found separately.
Keep the unrounded value on the calculator between stages and round **once**, at the end, to the accuracy asked for.
If no diagram is given, sketch one: mark the right angle first, then the known lengths and angles.
steps: Identify the right-angled triangles in the figure
Mark the unknown and any side the triangles share
Solve a triangle with a known side and acute angle, or two known sides; otherwise form and solve an equation involving both triangles
Carry any calculated length into the other triangle where needed
Answer the question that was asked

workedExamples.question_text:
A symmetrical tent end is $4$ m wide. Each sloping side makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with level ground. Find the height and the length of each sloping side, correct to $2$ decimal places.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(2,3.464)--cycle;\path (2,0) node[below] {$4\text{ m}$};\path (0.7,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
The central height divides the span into two bases of $2$ m.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(2,3.464)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (2,3.464)--(2,0);\draw (2,0.2)--(2.2,0.2)--(2.2,0);\path (1,0) node[below] {$2\text{ m}$};\path (2,1.7) node[right] {$h$};\path (1,1.732) node[above left] {$r$};\path (0.7,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\tan60^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{2}\\h&=2\tan60^{\circ}\\h&\approx3.46\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\cos60^{\circ}&=\frac{2}{r}\\r&=\frac{2}{\cos60^{\circ}}\\r&=4.00\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Each sloping side of a symmetrical A-frame tent is $3.2$ m long and makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with level ground. Find the width of the tent, correct to $2$ decimal places.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(3.2,0)--(1.6,2.771)--cycle;\path (0.8,1.386) node[above left] {$3.2\text{ m}$};\path (0.65,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
Draw the central height. Let $b$ be the base of one right-angled triangle; the tent width is $2b$.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(3.2,0)--(1.6,2.771)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (1.6,2.771)--(1.6,0);\draw (1.6,0.2)--(1.8,0.2)--(1.8,0);\path (0.8,0) node[below] {$b$};\path (0.8,1.386) node[above left] {$3.2\text{ m}$};\path (0.65,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\cos60^{\circ}&=\frac{b}{3.2}\\b&=3.2\cos60^{\circ}\\b&=1.6\text{ m}\\\text{Width}&=2b\\\text{Width}&=3.20\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the angle each sloping side makes with level ground in each symmetrical tent. Give both answers to $1$ decimal place.
(a) The width is $8$ m and the central height is $3$ m.
(b) The width is $8$ m and each sloping side is $5$ m.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(2,1.5)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (2,1.5)--(2,0);\draw (2,0.15)--(2.15,0.15)--(2.15,0);\path (0.65,0.2) node {$\theta$};\path (2,0) node[below] {$(a)\ 8\text{ m}$};\path (2,0.85) node[right] {$3\text{ m}$};\draw (6,0)--(10,0)--(8,1.5)--cycle;\path (6.65,0.2) node {$\theta$};\path (8,0) node[below] {$(b)\ 8\text{ m}$};\path (7,0.75) node[above left] {$5\text{ m}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
Each central height halves the width, giving an adjacent side of $4$ m.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(4,3)--cycle;\draw (3.75,0)--(3.75,0.25)--(4,0.25);\path (2,0) node[below] {$4\text{ m}$};\path (4,1.5) node[right] {$3\text{ m}\ (a)$};\path (2,1.5) node[above left] {$5\text{ m}\ (b)$};\path (0.8,0.3) node {$\theta$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
(a) Use the opposite and adjacent sides.
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{3}{4}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\\\theta&\approx36.9^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
(b) Use the adjacent side and hypotenuse.
$\begin{aligned}\cos\theta&=\frac{4}{5}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)\\\theta&\approx36.9^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A tree snaps into two perpendicular sections. Its fallen top touches level ground $14$ m from its base. The remaining section makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the ground. Find the original tree height, correct to $1$ decimal place.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (B) at (3,1.732);\coordinate (C) at (4,0);\draw (A)--(B)--(C)--cycle;\draw (2.827,1.632)--(2.927,1.459)--(3.1,1.559);\path (2,0) node[below] {$14\text{ m}$};\path (0.8,0.25) node {$30^{\circ}$};\path (A) node[left] {$A$};\path (B) node[above] {$B$};\path (C) node[right] {$C$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
The ground distance $AC$ is the hypotenuse. Add the two tree sections $AB$ and $BC$.
$\begin{aligned}\cos30^{\circ}&=\frac{AB}{14}\\AB&=14\cos30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\sin30^{\circ}&=\frac{BC}{14}\\BC&=14\sin30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Original height}&=14\cos30^{\circ}+14\sin30^{\circ}\\\text{Original height}&\approx19.1\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A triangular roof truss has a vertical post $CD$ meeting its horizontal base $AB$ at $D$. The left chord $AC$ is $16$ m long and makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the base. The right chord makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the base. Find $DB$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4.619,0)--(3.464,2)--cycle;\draw (3.464,2)--(3.464,0);\draw (3.464,0.2)--(3.664,0.2)--(3.664,0);\path (1.732,1) node[above left] {$16\text{ m}$};\path (0.8,0.25) node {$30^{\circ}$};\path (4.12,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\path (0,0) node[below] {$A$};\path (4.619,0) node[below] {$B$};\path (3.464,2) node[above] {$C$};\path (3.464,0) node[below] {$D$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
First find the shared post $CD$ using the left triangle.
$\begin{aligned}\sin30^{\circ}&=\frac{CD}{16}\\CD&=16\sin30^{\circ}\\CD&=8\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
In the right triangle, $CD$ is opposite $60^{\circ}$ and $DB$ is adjacent.
$\begin{aligned}\tan60^{\circ}&=\frac{8}{DB}\\DB&=\frac{8}{\tan60^{\circ}}\\DB&\approx4.62\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A roof has an off-centre ridge supported by a vertical post. The left rafter is $6$ m long and rises at $30^{\circ}$. The post meets the horizontal wall top $4$ m from the right wall. Find the right rafter's angle to the horizontal, correct to the nearest minute.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(5.519,0)--(3.119,1.8)--cycle;\draw (3.119,1.8)--(3.119,0);\draw (3.119,0.2)--(3.319,0.2)--(3.319,0);\path (1.56,0.9) node[above left] {$6\text{ m}$};\path (4.319,0) node[below] {$4\text{ m}$};\path (0.8,0.25) node {$30^{\circ}$};\path (4.8,0.25) node {$\theta$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
First find the shared post $h$.
$\begin{aligned}\sin30^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{6}\\h&=6\sin30^{\circ}\\h&=3\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
Use the post and the horizontal run in the right triangle.
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{3}{4}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\\\theta&=36.869897\ldots^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Convert the decimal part of the angle to minutes.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Minutes}&=0.869897\ldots\times60\\\text{Minutes}&=52.1938\ldots\end{aligned}$
$\theta\approx36^{\circ}52'$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A triangular truss has a vertical altitude of $4$ m. Its foot lies between the ends of the horizontal base. The sloping sides make angles of $30^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ with the base. Find the perimeter, correct to $2$ decimal places.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4.619,0)--(3.464,2)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (3.464,2)--(3.464,0);\draw (3.464,0.2)--(3.664,0.2)--(3.664,0);\path (3.464,1) node[right] {$4\text{ m}$};\path (0.8,0.25) node {$30^{\circ}$};\path (4.12,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
The altitude creates two right-angled triangles. Let their horizontal bases be $p$ and $q$, and their sloping sides be $r$ and $s$.
$\begin{aligned}\tan30^{\circ}&=\frac{4}{p}\\p&=\frac{4}{\tan30^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\tan60^{\circ}&=\frac{4}{q}\\q&=\frac{4}{\tan60^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\sin30^{\circ}&=\frac{4}{r}\\r&=\frac{4}{\sin30^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\sin60^{\circ}&=\frac{4}{s}\\s&=\frac{4}{\sin60^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$
Add both base sections and both sloping sides, keeping the calculator values unrounded.
$\begin{aligned}P&=p+q+r+s\\P&=\frac{4}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{4}{\tan60^{\circ}}+\frac{4}{\sin30^{\circ}}+\frac{4}{\sin60^{\circ}}\\P&\approx21.86\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
An observer at $D$ is $6$ m horizontally from the foot $C$ of a vertical mast. Points $A$ and $B$ lie on the mast, with $A$ above $B$. Their angles of elevation from $D$ are $60^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}$ respectively. Find $AB$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(3,0)--(3,5.196)--cycle;\draw (0,0)--(3,1.732);\draw (2.8,0)--(2.8,0.2)--(3,0.2);\path (1.5,0) node[below] {$6\text{ m}$};\path (0,0) node[left] {$D$};\path (3,0) node[right] {$C$};\path (3,1.732) node[right] {$B$};\path (3,5.196) node[right] {$A$};\draw (0.8,0) arc (0:30:0.8);\path (1.15,0.23) node {$30^{\circ}$};\draw (0.5,0) arc (0:60:0.5);\path (0.5,0.8) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
Both triangles have adjacent side $DC=6$ m. Find the two heights, then subtract.
$\begin{aligned}\tan60^{\circ}&=\frac{AC}{6}\\AC&=6\tan60^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\tan30^{\circ}&=\frac{BC}{6}\\BC&=6\tan30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}AB&=AC-BC\\AB&=6\tan60^{\circ}-6\tan30^{\circ}\\AB&\approx6.93\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A ladder rests against a vertical wall on level ground. Its foot is $180$ cm from the wall and it makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the ground. Draw a diagram and find the ladder length to the nearest cm.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The ladder is the hypotenuse $L$; the horizontal distance is adjacent to $60^{\circ}$.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(2,0)--(2,3.464)--cycle;\draw (1.8,0)--(1.8,0.2)--(2,0.2);\path (1,0) node[below] {$180\text{ cm}$};\path (1,1.732) node[above left] {$L$};\path (0.65,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\cos60^{\circ}&=\frac{180}{L}\\L&=\frac{180}{\cos60^{\circ}}\\L&=360\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A vertical mast $AB$ is $8$ m high, and $M$ is its midpoint. Point $C$ is on level ground $8$ m horizontally from the foot $A$. Is $\angle ACM$ exactly half of $\angle ACB$? Calculate both angles to $1$ decimal place to support your answer.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(4,4)--cycle;\draw (0,0)--(4,2);\draw (3.8,0)--(3.8,0.2)--(4,0.2);\path (2,0) node[below] {$8\text{ m}$};\path (4,1) node[right] {$4\text{ m}$};\path (4,3) node[right] {$4\text{ m}$};\path (0,0) node[left] {$C$};\path (4,0) node[below] {$A$};\path (4,2) node[right] {$M$};\path (4,4) node[above] {$B$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
The midpoint gives $AM=4$ m. Both triangles are right-angled at $A$.
$\begin{aligned}\tan\angle ACM&=\frac{4}{8}\\\angle ACM&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{8}\right)\\\angle ACM&\approx26.6^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\tan\angle ACB&=\frac{8}{8}\\\angle ACB&=45.0^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Half of $45^{\circ}$ is $22.5^{\circ}$. Since $26.6^{\circ}\ne22.5^{\circ}$, $\angle ACM$ is not half of $\angle ACB$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A drawbridge has two identical sections, each $x$ m long, hinged at opposite riverbanks. When lowered, they exactly span the river. When raised to $60^{\circ}$ above the horizontal, their tips are $14$ m apart. Find the river width, correct to $1$ decimal place.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw[dashed] (0,0)--(5,0);\draw[thick] (0,0)--(1.25,2.165);\draw[thick] (5,0)--(3.75,2.165);\draw[dashed] (1.25,2.165)--(3.75,2.165);\path (2.5,2.165) node[above] {$14\text{ m}$};\path (0.625,1.083) node[above left] {$x\text{ m}$};\path (4.375,1.083) node[above right] {$x\text{ m}$};\path (0.65,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\path (4.35,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
The lowered sections span $2x$ m. Each raised section has horizontal projection $x\cos60^{\circ}$.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(1.25,0)--(1.25,2.165)--cycle;\draw (1.05,0)--(1.05,0.2)--(1.25,0.2);\path (0.625,1.083) node[above left] {$x$};\path (0.625,0) node[below] {$x\cos60^{\circ}$};\path (0.55,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
Subtract both horizontal projections from the river width to obtain the gap.
$\begin{aligned}2x-2x\cos60^{\circ}&=14\\2x(1-\cos60^{\circ})&=14\\2x&=\frac{14}{1-\cos60^{\circ}}\\2x&=28\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
The river is $28.0$ m wide.

workedExamples.question_text:
A balloon is directly above a point between the ends of a straight, horizontal road $20$ m long. Its angles of elevation from the two ends are $30^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$. Find its height above the road, correct to $2$ decimal places.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(3,1.732)--cycle;\path (2,0) node[below] {$20\text{ m}$};\path (0.75,0.25) node {$30^{\circ}$};\path (3.55,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\path (3,1.732) node[above] {balloon};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
Draw the vertical height $h$. The two horizontal distances $p$ and $q$ add to $20$ m.
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(3,1.732)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (3,1.732)--(3,0);\draw (3,0.18)--(3.18,0.18)--(3.18,0);\path (1.5,0) node[below] {$p$};\path (3.5,0) node[below] {$q$};\path (3,0.85) node[left] {$h$};\path (0.75,0.25) node {$30^{\circ}$};\path (3.55,0.3) node {$60^{\circ}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\tan30^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{p}\\p&=\frac{h}{\tan30^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\tan60^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{q}\\q&=\frac{h}{\tan60^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$
Neither triangle alone determines $h$. Use the total road length.
$\begin{aligned}p+q&=20\\\frac{h}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{h}{\tan60^{\circ}}&=20\\h\left(\frac{1}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\tan60^{\circ}}\right)&=20\\h&=\frac{20}{\frac{1}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\tan60^{\circ}}}\\h&\approx8.66\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text:
A symmetrical gable roof spans $6$ m between two walls of equal height. Each sloping side makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal.
Find the slant height of one side of the roof, correct to $1$ decimal place.
foundation.solution_text:
The vertical from the ridge divides the span into two bases of $3$ m.
$\cos60^{\circ}=\frac{3}{r}$
$r=\frac{3}{\cos60^{\circ}}$
$=6\text{ m}$
The slant height is $6.0\text{ m}$.

foundation.question_text:
A tree snaps and its top touches the ground. The remaining section and the fallen section are perpendicular. The distance along the ground from the base of the tree to its fallen top is $10$ m, and the remaining section is inclined at $30^{\circ}$ to horizontal ground.
Find the height of the original tree, correct to $1$ decimal place.
foundation.solution_text:
The two tree sections are the legs of a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $10$ m.
Remaining section $=10\cos30^{\circ}=8.6602\ldots\text{ m}$.
Fallen section $=10\sin30^{\circ}=5\text{ m}$.
Original height $=8.6602\ldots+5=13.6602\ldots\text{ m}$.
The original tree was $13.7\text{ m}$ high.

foundation.question_text:
A triangular truss has a vertical post from its apex to the horizontal deck. The left chord is $8$ m long and makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the deck. The right chord makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the deck.
Find the horizontal distance from the foot of the post to the right-hand end of the deck, correct to $2$ decimal places.
foundation.solution_text:
First find the vertical post $h$.
$\sin30^{\circ}=\frac{h}{8}$
$h=8\sin30^{\circ}=4\text{ m}$.
For the right-hand triangle, $\tan45^{\circ}=\frac{4}{q}$.
$q=\frac{4}{\tan45^{\circ}}=4\text{ m}$.
The horizontal distance is $4.00\text{ m}$.

foundation.solution_text:

development.question_text:
A gable end has a vertical post from the ridge to the horizontal wall top. The left rafter is $12$ m long and rises at $30^{\circ}$; the right rafter rises at $45^{\circ}$.
Find the horizontal distance from the foot of the post to the right-hand wall, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
First find the shared post $h$.
$\sin30^{\circ}=\frac{h}{12}$
$h=12\sin30^{\circ}=6\text{ m}$.
Now use the right-hand triangle.
$\tan45^{\circ}=\frac{6}{q}$
$q=\frac{6}{\tan45^{\circ}}=6\text{ m}$.
The horizontal distance is $6.00\text{ m}$.

development.question_text:
A surveyor runs a straight horizontal traverse from $A$ to $B$. A boundary corner $C$ lies off the traverse, and its perpendicular foot $D$ lies between $A$ and $B$. The distance $AC$ is $20$ m, $\angle CAB=30^{\circ}$ and $\angle CBA=60^{\circ}$.
Find $DB$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
First find the shared perpendicular $CD$.
$\sin30^{\circ}=\frac{CD}{20}$
$CD=20\sin30^{\circ}=10\text{ m}$.
Now use the right-hand triangle.
$\tan60^{\circ}=\frac{10}{DB}$
$DB=\frac{10}{\tan60^{\circ}}=5.7735\ldots\text{ m}$.
$DB\approx5.77\text{ m}$.

development.question_text:
A triangular truss has a vertical altitude of $6$ m whose foot lies between the ends of its horizontal base. The sloping sides make angles of $30^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ with the base.
Find the perimeter of the triangle, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
The altitude divides the triangle into two right-angled triangles.
Left base $=\frac{6}{\tan30^{\circ}}=10.3923\ldots\text{ m}$.
Right base $=\frac{6}{\tan60^{\circ}}=3.4641\ldots\text{ m}$.
Left sloping side $=\frac{6}{\sin30^{\circ}}=12\text{ m}$.
Right sloping side $=\frac{6}{\sin60^{\circ}}=6.9282\ldots\text{ m}$.
Perimeter $=\frac{6}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{6}{\tan60^{\circ}}+\frac{6}{\sin30^{\circ}}+\frac{6}{\sin60^{\circ}}$.
Perimeter $=32.7846\ldots\text{ m}\approx32.78\text{ m}$.

development.question_text:
A point $D$ is $8$ m horizontally from the foot $C$ of a vertical mast. Points $A$ and $B$ lie on the mast, with $A$ above $B$. The angles of elevation from $D$ to $A$ and $B$ are $60^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$ respectively.
Find $AB$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
Both right-angled triangles have horizontal base $DC=8\text{ m}$.
$AC=8\tan60^{\circ}=13.8564\ldots\text{ m}$.
$BC=8\tan45^{\circ}=8\text{ m}$.
$AB=AC-BC=8\tan60^{\circ}-8\tan45^{\circ}$.
$AB=5.8564\ldots\text{ m}\approx5.86\text{ m}$.

development.question_text:
A ladder rests against a vertical wall on level ground. Its foot is $240$ cm from the wall and it makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the ground.
Draw a diagram, then calculate the length of the ladder to the nearest cm.
development.solution_text:
Sketch a right-angled triangle with the wall vertical, the ground horizontal and the ladder as the hypotenuse $L$.
$\cos60^{\circ}=\frac{240}{L}$
$L=\frac{240}{\cos60^{\circ}}=480\text{ cm}$.
The ladder is $480\text{ cm}$ long.

development.question_text:
A vertical mast $AB$ is $12$ m high and $M$ is its midpoint. Point $C$ is on level ground $12$ m horizontally from the foot $A$.
Determine whether $\angle ACM$ is exactly half of $\angle ACB$. Calculate both angles to $1$ decimal place to support your answer.
development.solution_text:
$AM=6\text{ m}$ and both triangles are right-angled at $A$.
$\tan\angle ACM=\frac{6}{12}$, so $\angle ACM=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{12}\right)=26.5650\ldots^{\circ}\approx26.6^{\circ}$.
$\tan\angle ACB=\frac{12}{12}$, so $\angle ACB=45.0^{\circ}$.
Half of $\angle ACB$ is $22.5^{\circ}$, so $\angle ACM$ is not exactly half of $\angle ACB$.

[/tikz]
A drawbridge is made of two identical sections, each $x$ m long, hinged at opposite banks of a river.
Lowered, the two sections exactly span the river.
Raised to $52^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, their tips are $15$ m apart.
Find the width of the river, correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
Lowered, the sections span the river, so the river is $2x$ m wide.
Raised, each section covers a horizontal distance of $x\cos52^{\circ}$, and what is left over is the gap.
$2x-2x\cos52^{\circ}=15$
$2x(1-\cos52^{\circ})=15$
$2x=\frac{15}{1-\cos52^{\circ}}$
$=39.0280\ldots$
$\approx39.0\text{ m}$

The end wall of a shed is $7.4$ m wide.
Its left rafter rises at $48^{\circ}$ and its right rafter at $33^{\circ}$.
Find the height of the ridge above the wall top, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
Dropping the vertical from the ridge makes two right-angled triangles whose bases add to $7.4$ m.
$\tan48^{\circ}=\frac{h}{p}$, so $p=\frac{h}{\tan48^{\circ}}$
$\tan33^{\circ}=\frac{h}{q}$, so $q=\frac{h}{\tan33^{\circ}}$
$\frac{h}{\tan48^{\circ}}+\frac{h}{\tan33^{\circ}}=7.4$
$h\left(\frac{1}{\tan48^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\tan33^{\circ}}\right)=7.4$
$h=\frac{7.4}{2.4402\ldots}$
$=3.0324\ldots$
$\approx3.03\text{ m}$

mastery.question_text:
From the ends of a straight horizontal road $12$ m long, a balloon directly above a point between the ends is observed at angles of elevation of $30^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$.
Find the height of the balloon above the road, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
Draw a vertical from the balloon to the road. Let the height be $h$ and the two horizontal distances be $p$ and $q$.
$\tan30^{\circ}=\frac{h}{p}$, so $p=\frac{h}{\tan30^{\circ}}$.
$\tan60^{\circ}=\frac{h}{q}$, so $q=\frac{h}{\tan60^{\circ}}$.
Since $p+q=12$, $h\left(\frac{1}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\tan60^{\circ}}\right)=12$.
$h=\frac{12}{\frac{1}{\tan30^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\tan60^{\circ}}}=5.1961\ldots\text{ m}$.
The balloon is $5.20\text{ m}$ above the road.
